result.markdown: --- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Comparison.status_counts]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} | Pointblank description: The number of test units with each row status. twitter-card: title: >- [Comparison.status_counts]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} | Pointblank description: The number of test units with each row status. title: >- [Comparison.status_counts]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: The number of test units with each row status. page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} The number of test units with each row status. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [Comparison.status_counts]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[str, int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ::: {.doc-text} Where [`n_passed`](`pointblank.Comparison.n_passed`) and [`n_failed`](`pointblank.Comparison.n_failed`) say how many rows differ, `status_counts` says how they differ. The statuses are described in the *Test Units and Row Statuses* section of [`compare()`](`pointblank.compare`). The counts are computed when the comparison is made, so reading them doesn't touch the tables again. The counts are the row statuses alone and aren't affected by the schema check. If the schema check fails, there can be `"match"` rows even though no test units pass. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} In this example, station `S3` appears twice in the source table. ::: {#8e66d312 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pointblank as pb import polars as pl readings_v1 = pl.DataFrame( {"station": ["S1", "S2", "S3", "S3", "S4"], "temp": [12.1, 14.0, 9.8, 9.9, 11.2]} ) readings_v2 = pl.DataFrame( {"station": ["S1", "S2", "S3", "S5"], "temp": [12.1, 14.3, 9.8, 8.0]} ) comparison = pb.compare(readings_v1, readings_v2, keys="station") comparison.status_counts ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {'match': 1, 'changed': 1, 'missing': 1, 'extra': 1, 'dup_key': 2} ``` ::: ::: Each status has a different cause. `S2` changed, `S4` is missing from the target, and `S5` is extra. The duplicated `S3` key counts as two `"dup_key"` units, since it occurs twice in the source. Those rows can't be paired up, so they're not compared. To see the rows behind any of these counts, pass the status to [`rows()`](`pointblank.Comparison.rows`), as in `comparison.rows("dup_key")`.
